title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
abstract: arXiv:2611.32823v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems for computed tomography (CT) remain largely restricted to specific anatomical regions, examination types or predefined abnormalities, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive and spatially grounded interpretations. Here we present FORA, a general-purpose CT model that recognizes and spatially localizes 1,028 hierarchically organized radiological concepts and generates reports across the 28 CT protocols represented in our cohort. Trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations supervised by their accompanying reports, FORA learns to localize abnormalities without manually annotated lesions. Its architecture combines multiple-instance learning with an interpretable concept bottleneck that connects spatial evidence, radiological findings and report generation. We first developed and benchmarked the architecture on chest radiographs, achieving state-of-the-art performance, before training a separate model

translated_title: FORA：实现任意计算机断层扫描的可靠且有定位依据的报告生成
translated_abstract: 用于计算机断层扫描（CT）的人工智能系统在很大程度上仍然局限于特定的解剖区域、检查类型或预定义的异常，这限制了它们提供全面且具有空间定位依据的解读能力。在此，我们提出了FORA，一个通用CT模型，它能够识别1,028个分层组织的放射学概念并对其进行空间定位，并为我们队列中涵盖的28种CT检查方案生成报告。FORA在304,962例常规CT检查及其随附报告的监督下进行训练，无需人工标注病灶即可学会定位异常。其架构将多示例学习与可解释的概念瓶颈相结合，连接了空间证据、放射学发现与报告生成。我们首先在胸片上开发并对该架构进行了基准测试，取得了最先进的性能，随后训练了一个单独的模型
tldr: 提出通用CT模型FORA，可识别并空间定位1,028个放射学概念、覆盖28种CT检查方案自动生成报告，无需人工标注病灶即可学习异常定位，并在胸片基准测试中达到最先进性能。
en_tdlr: FORA is a general-purpose CT model that recognizes and spatially localizes 1,028 radiological concepts across 28 CT protocols, learns to localize abnormalities without manually annotated lesions, and achieves state-of-the-art performance benchmarked on chest radiographs.
